output.abstract_summary: The paper introduces GEPA (Genetic-Pareto), a prompt optimizer that leverages natural language reflection to learn high-level rules from trial and error, rather than relying on sparse scalar rewards used by RL methods like GRPO. GEPA samples trajectories from LLM prompts, reflects on them in natural language to diagnose problems, proposes and tests prompt updates, and combines complementary lessons from the Pareto frontier. Across six tasks, GEPA outperforms GRPO by 6% on average (up to 20%) using up to 35x fewer rollouts, and surpasses MIPROv2 by over 10% (e.g., +12% accuracy on AIME-2025).

output.description: This flowchart illustrates the GEPA algorithm's iterative candidate generation and evaluation process, including candidate proposal via Reflective Prompt Mutation or System Aware Merge, minibatch evaluation, performance-based retention, and Pareto-based filtering to maintain diversity across tasks.
findings: GEPA iteratively generates new candidates using either Reflective Prompt Mutation or System Aware Merge strategies.
Candidates are first evaluated on a minibatch; only those showing improvement proceed to full evaluation and are added to the candidate pool.
The algorithm avoids local optima by employing Pareto-based sampling, selecting diverse candidates per task rather than always mutating the single best performer.
The Scores Matrix and Pareto Filtering ensure that candidate selection maintains cross-task diversity while preserving high-performing individuals.
